Katherine: FYI - new starter template (Next + LangChain wiring) is tripping on the eval harness during edge preview. Quick notes below.
Ibrahim: Steps to repro?
Katherine: Clone repo, npm ci, set RW_API_KEY, deploy with Vercel Edge target or run `vercel dev --edge`. Then run the provided eval runner against /api/chat. On node runtime everything passes, on edge the harness reports missing stream chunks and sporadic 401s on the first call after refresh.
Lena: Which SDK and starter commit?
Katherine: @redwood/sdk 0.10.1, starter commit bb9f3. Next 13.5. Repro locally with `vercel dev` too.
Carlos: Any logs/snippets?
Katherine: Paste: 
```
WARN sdk: transport: selected=node-polyfill
Error: EvalHarness: timed out waiting for first chunk
    at harness.waitForStream (/workspace/eval/index.js:56:10)
TypeError: Auth: token missing on first request
    at refreshToken (/workspace/node_modules/@redwood/sdk/dist/auth.js:88:14)
```
Ibrahim: Two likely problems: (1) bundler included Node stream polyfill instead of using platform ReadableStream, (2) auth cache/refresh race across edge invocations.
Lena: Did the sample call await init(...) in the handler? Edge cold starts need explicit await.
Katherine: The sample had `init(...)` without await to keep examples compact.
Carlos: That's an easy doc fix: update sample to `await init(...)` in API handlers. But the underlying SDK behavior should be robust even if people call init() without await.
Ibrahim: Agreed. SDK should be idempotent and provide isReady() so examples can choose a terse or explicit pattern. Also the transport selection should prefer native ReadableStream when available and only fall back to polyfill for Node-targeted builds.
Lena: For auth: edge runtimes isolate each request, so a global in-memory token cache isn't reliable across invocations. We should add a request-scoped tokenProvider hook to init({ tokenProvider }) so starters and middleware can surface request cookies or a per-request store.
Katherine: I tried a quick hack: changed handler to `await init()` and wired a tokenProvider that reads/writes to req.cookies. The 401-on-first-call stopped. Streaming still flaky though.
Carlos: Good diagnostic. For streaming: can you share bundled files or the build log that shows node-polyfill included?
Katherine: Pasted gist with bundle listing: https://gist.github.com/redwood-repro/edge-starter-bundle. It lists node-stream-polyfill under @redwood/sdk/dist.
Ibrahim: We'll update the SDK build to mark stream polyfill as optional and add runtime detection: prefer global.ReadableStream/TransformStream, otherwise try WebStream polyfill, else Node. Also add a clear log line showing the selected transport so people can debug quickly.
Lena: And tests: add unit tests that simulate envs with and without globals: set global.ReadableStream = undefined and ensure fallback works, and add an emulated edge test for tokenProvider flow to catch the 401 race.
Carlos: For samples, I'll open a PR that: (1) changes handler to await init, (2) includes a commented tokenProvider example for Next edge, and (3) adds a troubleshooting note in README about bundler target and monorepo pitfalls.
Katherine: Created minimal failing handler pasted into the ticket: 
```js
import { init, chat } from '@redwood/sdk'
export default async function handler(req) {
  await init({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY })
  // tokenProvider example (optional):
  // await init({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY, tokenProvider: {
  //  get: () => req.cookies['rw_token'],
  //  set: (t) => {/* set cookie on response in middleware */}
  // }})
  const resp = await chat(req.body)
  return new Response(resp.body)
}
```
build-bot: Created ticket DEVEX-3417: "edge-starter - streaming transport + request tokenProvider" assigned to @Ibrahim and @Lena.
Ibrahim: I'll open an SDK PR to: (A) prefer native streams, (B) make init idempotent + add isReady(), (C) expose tokenProvider option.
Lena: I'll add tests and update the sample README with explicit edge notes. Also will add a small sample showing how to use tokenProvider with Next middleware so onboarding is less friction.
Katherine: Thanks 44d I'll validate once PRs land and re-run the eval harness on Vercel.
Carlos: Small follow-up: add a short snippet in the quickstart that explains when to choose Edge vs Server runtime for starters (tradeoffs for eval harness and streaming). Many users pick Edge by default and then hit these quirks.
Katherine: Agreed, I'll add that to the PR too.
Ibrahim: ETA: SDK PR by EOD tomorrow, sample updates after that.
Katherine: Great, thanks all.
